notes: Direct HTTP fetch worked throughout (no WAF, consistent with prior Home-Decor pass for this company). Discovered via sitemaps/collections.xml.gz (2528 URLs) and confirmed via the site's own embedded breadcrumb/taxonomy JSON on each page (a Next.js-style flattened object graph containing 'breadcrumbs'/'treeLevel'/'taxonId' keys). This revealed a genuine 2-level site-defined hierarchy directly under New Arrivals (taxonId 5050): two 'main'-level children -- 'New Arrivals 2' (taxonId 9590, a second distinct new-arrivals batch/collection, different product count from the parent) and 'Shop by Styles' (taxonId 9463, itself a real PLP AND the parent of 10 'sub'-level style-filtered leaf pages: Japandi, Scandinavian, Mid-Century Modern, Beach Resort, Minimalist, Eclectic, Biophilic Design, Bauhaus, Dopamine Decor, Wabi Sabi). Every one of these was opened and confirmed to be a real browsable product grid (not an editorial/lookbook page) carrying the site's own exact '(N items)' breadcrumb count -- same qty-source methodology verified reliable in the prior Home-Decor pass for hipvan.com. Per the brief's 'Collection pages need inspection every time' rule, each style page's product grid + pagination + exact count was checked before inclusion; none were marketing-only landing pages. No other New Arrivals-type terms (New In, Just Arrived, Latest Arrivals, What's New, Recently Added) were found anywhere in the sitemap, pages.xml (CMS pages), homepage nav, or footer -- /new-arrivals and its two 'main' children above are the complete New Arrivals surface on hipvan.com. The top-level /new-arrivals row (406 items) is itself a genuine independent product listing (title 'Buy New Furniture Online in Singapore') in addition to being the nav parent of the two children below it, so it is recorded with is_group=true to reflect that it has site-defined children, while still carrying its own real qty.
